title: AP Chinese Language and Culture
summary: Interpret Mandarin text, connect ideas and write precise responses using original cultural scenarios.
frameworkNote: Checked against the revised 2026-27 framework on 15 October 2026: six thematic units and a course project supporting exam speaking tasks. The 2027 project packet is due for release in January 2027. These original fictional text scenarios are practice, not authentic cultural sources or a completed project. Add authentic target-language research, listening, conversation and teacher feedback; text answers do not assess pronunciation or oral proficiency. Examples use simplified characters; learners may consult their course guidance on accepted script.

modules.title: Read a neighbourhood invitation
modules.focus: Families and communities: distinguish dates, frequency and obligation.
explanation: Chinese time expressions normally appear before the main verb. “我们星期六在社区中心见面” means “We will meet at the community centre on Saturday.” The time and place establish the setting before 见面. A notice may omit a subject when the context makes it clear.

Read restrictions carefully: “请提前报名” asks people to register in advance, while “每月一次” means once a month. Do not infer a weekly event from a familiar-looking number. In cultural discussion, a fictional neighbourhood activity illustrates language use, not a universal family practice.

workedExample.prompt: Reply to a fictional notice: “周六举行读书活动，请提前报名。”
steps: Identify the activity and day: a reading event on Saturday.
Ask “请问，我应该怎么报名？” meaning “May I ask how I should register?”

misconception.claim: Chinese needs a tense ending on every future verb.
misconception.correction: Time words and context can locate an event without conjugating the verb.

questions.prompt: Interpret “活动每月举行一次”.
questions.hint: 每月 gives the period; 一次 gives the frequency.
questions.answer: The activity is held once a month.

questions.prompt: Ask politely whether parents can participate.
questions.answer: “请问，家长也可以参加吗？” (May I ask whether parents can participate too?)

questions.prompt: Interpret “最好带水，但必须穿运动鞋”.
questions.hint: Distinguish 最好 and 必须.
hints: Distinguish 最好 and 必须.
questions.answer: Bringing water is recommended. Sports shoes are required. The sentence does not make the water recommendation compulsory.
checkpoints: The sentence does not make the water recommendation compulsory.

questions.prompt: Ask politely in Chinese whether materials are provided.
questions.answer: “请问，活动提供材料吗？” The question asks about materials. It clarifies what the participant may need to bring.
checkpoints: It clarifies what the participant may need to bring.

notes.title: Read a neighbourhood invitation in depth
paragraphs: An invitation may give an activity date and a separate registration deadline. 星期三以前 means before Wednesday, whereas 从星期三开始 marks a starting point. 必须 expresses necessity, 可以 permission or possibility, and 最好 a recommendation. A courteous reply should identify the intended activity and ask about a missing practical detail. 请问 introduces a question politely but does not itself answer the organiser's request. Reading these small expressions accurately prevents a learner from confusing advice with obligation or treating the registration day as the day of the event.

workedExamples.prompt: Original notice: “星期五下午举行手工活动，请在星期三以前报名，并带一把剪刀。” Reply.
steps: The activity is Friday afternoon; registration is before Wednesday and scissors are requested.
“我想参加星期五的手工活动。请问，活动几点开始？我会带剪刀。”
workedExamples.conclusion: The reply confirms the activity and asks for the missing start time.

flashcards.back: May or can, according to context.

flashcards.front: 星期三以前是什么意思？

diagrams.title: 活动和报名
diagrams.description: 两个时间表达不同的安排。

modules.title: Connect contrast and language choice
modules.focus: Language and culture: follow concession and perspective.
explanation: “虽然……但是……” connects a concession with a contrasting main point. “虽然这个词很流行，但是老人不一定明白” means that although the word is popular, older people may not necessarily understand it. “不一定” limits certainty; it does not mean that nobody understands.

Avoid using one phrase as evidence about all Chinese-speaking communities. Language varies by setting, generation and individual experience. Attribute a view with “作者认为” (the author thinks) or “根据这篇文章” (according to this article), then distinguish the source’s evidence from your own interpretation.

workedExample.prompt: Interpret “这个说法很方便，不过正式邮件里不太合适。”
steps: Identify the benefit: the expression is convenient.
Identify the limit introduced by 不过: it is not very suitable in a formal email. The sentence does not ban it everywhere.

misconception.correction: It means not necessarily and leaves room for different cases.

questions.prompt: Translate the force of “大家不一定同意”.
questions.hint: Focus on certainty, not word-for-word order.
questions.answer: Not everyone necessarily agrees, or people may not all agree.

questions.prompt: Attribute the view that a word’s meaning is clear.
questions.answer: “作者认为这个词的意思很清楚。” (The author thinks the meaning of this word is clear.)

questions.prompt: Interpret “有人觉得方便，我却觉得不够清楚”.
questions.answer: Some people find it convenient. The speaker finds it insufficiently clear. The sentence presents differing views without measuring their prevalence.
checkpoints: The speaker finds it insufficiently clear.
The sentence presents differing views without measuring their prevalence.

questions.prompt: Write a Chinese observation about one student's language choice without generalising.
questions.answer: “在这个例子中，学生给老师写信时用了比较正式的表达。” The claim concerns this example. It does not describe every student's language.
checkpoints: “在这个例子中，学生给老师写信时用了比较正式的表达。”
It does not describe every student's language.

notes.title: Connect contrast and language choice in depth
paragraphs: Attribution separates a source's opinion from the writer's judgement. 作者认为 introduces what the author thinks, while 我觉得 identifies the current speaker's view. 不一定 limits certainty and differs from 一定不, which can express a definite negative judgement in context. A concession with 虽然 recognises one point before another is introduced by 但是. Keep the scope attached to the evidence: a phrase may suit messages between friends while being unsuitable in a particular report. This is a contextual language choice, not proof that an entire generation speaks identically.

workedExamples.prompt: Original text: “虽然这个词很常见，但是小林觉得它不适合正式报告。”
steps: The sentence accepts that the word is common.
小林觉得 attributes the judgement about formal reports to Xiaolin.
workedExamples.conclusion: The objection concerns a context, not the word's use everywhere.

diagrams.title: 常见不等于适用
diagrams.description: 语言选择取决于具体场合。

nodes.label: 小林的判断
nodes.detail: 认为该词在这里不合适。

modules.title: Study a musical practice with evidence
modules.focus: Art and creativity: distinguish practice from interpretation.
explanation: A musical instrument or recording is a cultural product, while rehearsing or performing is a practice. A participant’s explanation can supply evidence about perspective. These categories help organise an argument, but no object automatically proves what an entire community values.

For authentic project research, record the source creator, date, community and relevant passage or timestamp. Use Chinese sources and paraphrase accurately. The fictional interview below is only a reading exercise. It cannot replace actual listening, source research or the official project packet released for the exam year.

workedExample.prompt: Read the fictional statement: “我们每周排练，不只是为了演出，也是为了认识邻居。”
steps: Identify the repeated practice: rehearsing every week.
Explain the two purposes: preparing for performance and getting to know neighbours. Do not reduce it to entertainment alone.

misconception.claim: A performance has only one purpose.
misconception.correction: Participants can describe several social or artistic purposes.

questions.prompt: What does “认识邻居” add to the statement?
questions.answer: It identifies getting to know neighbours as a social purpose.
checkpoints: Keeps it attributed to the group

questions.prompt: Write a short Chinese paraphrase of the social purpose.
questions.answer: “他们通过排练认识邻居。” (They get to know neighbours through rehearsing.)

questions.prompt: Paraphrase “我们改了节奏，但没有改歌词”.
questions.answer: “节奏发生了变化。” “歌词保持不变。” The statement does not specify a new melody.
checkpoints: The statement does not specify a new melody.

questions.prompt: Explain in Chinese why a concert poster cannot alone establish listeners' feelings.
questions.hint: Identify what a poster usually records.
hints: Identify what a poster usually records.
questions.answer: “海报可以提供时间和演出者等信息。” “它不一定记录听众的感受。” “研究听众的看法还需要相关的采访或调查。”
checkpoints: “海报可以提供时间和演出者等信息。”
“研究听众的看法还需要相关的采访或调查。”

notes.title: Study a musical practice with evidence in depth
paragraphs: A musical research note should preserve the difference between an action, a purpose and an observed outcome. 为了 introduces purpose; 已经 can mark that an event has already occurred, but a factual claim still needs a source. 每两周一次 means once every two weeks, unlike 每周两次, twice a week. Accurate frequency matters when describing a practice. A recording can support observations about musical sound, while an interview can support an attributed explanation of meaning. Neither alone shows what every listener or member of a community believes.

workedExamples.prompt: Original invented interview: “我们每两周排练一次，为了让新成员熟悉这些歌曲。”
steps: The group rehearses once every two weeks.
Paraphrase: “排练的目的是帮助新成员熟悉歌曲。”
workedExamples.conclusion: The statement explains rehearsal frequency and purpose, not the number of successful performances.

flashcards.front: 每两周一次是什么意思？

flashcards.back: 受访者表达的观点和经历。

diagrams.title: 排练与新成员
diagrams.description: 虚构采访解释一种具体做法。

modules.title: Interpret data and a technological limit
modules.focus: Science and technology: report proportions accurately.
explanation: Chinese percentages place 百分之 before the number: 百分之三十 means thirty percent. The denominator still matters. “受访者的百分之三十” refers to thirty percent of respondents, not thirty percent of all residents.

An argument should distinguish possible effects from observed ones. “可能” expresses possibility; “已经” signals that something has already happened, though a factual claim still requires evidence. When discussing a fictional app trial, report the measured group and consider access for people without reliable devices or connectivity.

workedExample.prompt: In a fictional survey, 12 of 40 respondents use a transport app.
steps: Calculate 12 ÷ 40 = 0.30.
Write “百分之三十的受访者使用这个应用。” (Thirty percent of respondents use this app.)

misconception.claim: A numerical claim is representative regardless of the sample.
misconception.correction: The sample and survey method determine what population can reasonably be discussed.

questions.prompt: Express 25% in Chinese.
questions.hint: Use 百分之 followed by the number.
questions.answer: 百分之二十五.

questions.prompt: Make “这个工具提高效率” a cautious prediction.
questions.answer: “这个工具可能提高效率。” (This tool may improve efficiency.)
checkpoints: Does not claim a measured improvement

questions.prompt: Report 6 of 30 respondents having difficulty using an app in Chinese.
questions.answer: “百分之二十的受访者使用这个应用时遇到困难。” 6/30 equals 20%. The finding applies to respondents, not automatically all residents.
checkpoints: “百分之二十的受访者使用这个应用时遇到困难。”
The finding applies to respondents, not automatically all residents.

questions.prompt: Explain why 100 downloads do not establish 100 satisfied users.
questions.answer: “下载次数不等于不同用户的人数。” “下载也不能证明用户满意。” “需要询问实际使用者的体验，并说明调查范围。”
checkpoints: “下载次数不等于不同用户的人数。”
“需要询问实际使用者的体验，并说明调查范围。”

notes.title: Interpret data and a technological limit in depth
paragraphs: A proportion compares a part with a stated whole. The expression 受访者中 identifies a surveyed group; it must not disappear when a statistic is paraphrased. 使用次数 counts uses, while 使用人数 counts people, so repeated activity by one person can affect the first without increasing the second. 从百分之二十增加到百分之三十 is an increase of ten percentage points and fifty percent relative to the original value. Keep prediction and measurement separate: 可能提高效率 proposes an effect, whereas a demonstrated efficiency claim needs an appropriate comparison.

workedExamples.prompt: Invented data: 10 of 25 respondents use a tool; later 10 of 20 do.
steps: Calculate 40% and 50%, with ten users in both samples.
“使用者的比例提高了十个百分点，但人数仍然是十人。”
workedExamples.conclusion: A changing denominator explains the higher percentage.

flashcards.front: 使用次数和使用人数相同吗？
flashcards.back: 不同，次数可以包括重复使用。
可能性，而不是已证实的结果。

diagrams.title: 人数和比例
diagrams.description: 分母变化会改变百分比。

modules.title: Explain a routine that changed
modules.focus: Contemporary life: use aspect and temporal sequence.
explanation: “以前” establishes an earlier situation and “现在” contrasts the present. “以前我骑车上学，现在我坐公交车” compares two routines without needing a past-tense ending on 骑. Chinese aspect markers and time expressions do different jobs.

了 can mark a completed event or a changed situation depending on placement and context. It is not a universal equivalent of English past tense. To explain a daily-life change, identify the event, its consequence and the relevant timeframe; keep a personal example distinct from a claim about everyone’s lifestyle.

workedExample.prompt: Describe a commute change after moving home.
steps: State “我搬家了。” (I have moved home.)
Add “以前我走路上学，现在坐公交车。” (I used to walk to school; now I take the bus.)

misconception.claim: Every sentence about the past must contain 了.
misconception.correction: Habitual or background past statements can be expressed with time context and no 了.

questions.prompt: Interpret “以前我每天去图书馆”.
questions.hint: 以前 and 每天 establish the routine.
questions.answer: I used to go to the library every day.

questions.prompt: Connect a late bus to arriving late using 因为 and 所以.
questions.answer: “因为公交车晚点，所以我迟到了。” (Because the bus was delayed, I arrived late.)

questions.prompt: Interpret “我以前坐公交车，现在走路上学”.
questions.answer: The speaker used to take the bus. Now the speaker walks to school. This is the speaker's routine, not a claim about every pupil.
checkpoints: The speaker used to take the bus.
Now the speaker walks to school.
This is the speaker's routine, not a claim about every pupil.

questions.prompt: Write a Chinese account with a move and its consequence.
questions.hint: Use 搬家 and 现在.
hints: Use 搬家 and 现在.
questions.answer: “我去年搬家了。” “现在学校离家更近，我可以走路上学。” The consequence follows from the shorter distance.
checkpoints: “现在学校离家更近，我可以走路上学。”
The consequence follows from the shorter distance.

notes.title: Explain a routine that changed in depth
paragraphs: Chinese time expressions and aspect markers do different work. 以前 sets an earlier situation, 后来 advances a sequence, and 现在 establishes the present. 过 often marks an experience, as in 我去过那家图书馆, while a sentence-final 了 can signal a changed situation, as in 我现在住得更近了. Neither is simply an English past-tense ending. Build an account by naming a prior routine, the change and its consequence. A learner should preserve the timeframe explicitly instead of attaching 了 mechanically to every verb describing the past.

workedExamples.prompt: Describe a fictional change after a new library opens.
steps: “以前我在家看书。” gives the prior routine.
“附近开了一家图书馆。现在我每周去那里两次。” gives a change and present frequency.
workedExamples.conclusion: The sequence explains the routine without making a claim about all residents.

diagrams.title: 日常活动的改变
diagrams.description: 时间词连接过去与现在。

nodes.label: 新图书馆
nodes.detail: 附近出现了新的学习地点。

modules.title: State a conditional proposal
modules.focus: Global contexts: define the action and expected outcome.
explanation: “如果……就……” links a condition with a consequence. “如果学校增加回收箱，学生就更容易分类” means that if the school adds recycling bins, sorting will become easier for students. This is a proposed mechanism, not evidence that the outcome has happened.

A recommendation should also consider implementation. Labels, collection arrangements and participation can affect whether a recycling scheme works. Use specific measures to evaluate a trial, and distinguish the quantity collected from the amount successfully recycled.

workedExample.prompt: Propose a fictional school sorting trial.
steps: Write “如果垃圾箱的标志更清楚，学生就更容易分类。”
Explain that clearer bin labels may make sorting easier; test contamination rates before claiming improved recycling.

misconception.claim: More collection bins necessarily mean more material is recycled.
misconception.correction: Collection, sorting quality and processing capacity all affect the final outcome.

questions.prompt: What does 如果 introduce?
questions.hint: Look at the relationship between clauses.
questions.answer: A condition, often translated as if.
checkpoints: Does not confuse it with because

questions.prompt: Name a useful measure for the fictional sorting trial.
questions.hint: Count errors as well as collected material.
questions.answer: The proportion of incorrectly sorted items in comparable samples before and after clearer labels.

questions.prompt: Write a conditional Chinese proposal for clearer recycling labels.
questions.answer: “如果标志更清楚，学生就更容易分类。” The condition concerns label clarity. Sorting accuracy still needs observation before success is claimed.
checkpoints: “如果标志更清楚，学生就更容易分类。”
Sorting accuracy still needs observation before success is claimed.

questions.prompt: Explain one condition for a reusable-cup trial in Chinese.
questions.answer: “必须安排清洗和归还。” “发出多少杯子不等于少用了多少一次性杯子。” “应比较实际使用情况和废弃物数量。”
checkpoints: “发出多少杯子不等于少用了多少一次性杯子。”
“应比较实际使用情况和废弃物数量。”

notes.title: State a conditional proposal in depth
paragraphs: A proposal becomes assessable when it identifies an action, the intermediate change it should produce and the result to measure. 如果 can introduce a condition, while 为了 states an aim and 建议 marks a recommendation. These expressions do not turn a predicted benefit into an observation. A repair activity may extend an object's life, but counting participants does not establish that replacement purchases fell. Include tools, supervision and access in the proposal, then distinguish successful repairs from objects that still need replacement. This keeps the argument specific enough to evaluate.

workedExamples.prompt: Propose a fictional school bag-repair activity.
steps: “我建议学校组织修理书包的活动。”
“如果有合适的工具和指导，旧书包可能可以继续使用。”
workedExamples.conclusion: Record which repairs last before claiming reduced purchases.

flashcards.front: 参加人数能证明少买书包吗？
flashcards.back: 不能，需要了解修理和后续使用。

diagrams.title: 修理与继续使用
diagrams.description: 效果取决于中间步骤是否成功。
